verdict.rationale: Smithery's own docs say each published server gets a dedicated server page where users can 'discover, try, and install' it. That is only a thin hint of a browser-based way to exercise tools. The October 31, 2026 shutdown of the proxied Connect/API services, leaving only a non-proxied registry, makes it doubtful this still works. The CLI's 'smithery tool call' is a terminal surface, not a browser inspector, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of a browser inspector/playground that lists and invokes tools, evidence it survives the service shutdown, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can exercise an MCP server's tools from a browser-based inspector or playground before integrating it

citations.quote: Get a dedicated server page where users can discover, try, and install your MCP from any client
